title: Two neighbors
text: Two power companies share a river, but plan their work without seeing each other. The Savannah River is the border: Georgia Power builds on the Georgia side, Dominion Energy on the South Carolina side.

title: Their plans
text: Dominion plans 54 jobs. Georgia Power plans 60. Nobody lines them up. MrGridy put every one of them on one map, from their public filings.

title: Where they collide
text: Of 2,580 possible pairs, only 50 are within a crew's morning drive, forty kilometers. Two of them touch outright.

title: The best match
text: These two jobs touch. One crew, one yard, one permit instead of two. Dominion's Okatie to McIntosh 115 kilovolt Tie, and Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh expansion. Both are under construction at the same time for about 7 months.

title: What it saves
text: What working together could save: roughly $2.1 million across all 50 matches, somewhere between $1 million and $3.1 million. It is an estimate. Georgia Power does not publish its project costs, so real savings could be higher.

title: When a storm comes
text: About 55 hours before Hurricane Helene arrived, MrGridy predicted where lines would break for both companies, and compared it with what happened. It simulated the storm 10,000 times, with physics.

title: Fix it together
text: Working together, power comes back about 11 hours sooner, and 2.5 hours sooner for people who rely on powered medical equipment. Shared staging yards and crews go to the nearest repair zone first, whichever company owns it. Two neighbors, one plan.

title: Corridor fly-through
text: This is the number one match, near Rincon, Georgia. In teal, DESC's Okatie to McIntosh 115 kilovolt Tie. In orange, Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh expansion. Here the two projects touch, so their outages have to be planned together. They could share outage coordination, right-of-way, access roads and permits. One staging yard, right beside both jobs, would serve both crews. And for about 7 months, both crews are due to be here at the same time.

title: Storm crew briefing: Helene
text: Storm crew briefing for Hurricane Helene. On the Georgia side, the heaviest outages are expected in Fulton County, Richmond County and Lowndes County, with about 802,000 customers out across Georgia at the peak. On the South Carolina side, watch Greenville County, Richland County and Lexington County, with about 381,000 customers out statewide. The simulation expects roughly 1,100 damaged transmission sections on Georgia Power's system and 140 on DESC's. Both utilities stage jointly at I 520 bridge over the Savannah River, which reaches one repair zone within 38 minutes and I 95 bridge over the Savannah River, which reaches four repair zones within 59 minutes. Vulnerable areas first. Start near Richmond County, where about 5,000 residents rely on powered medical equipment, then Effingham County and Coffee County. Working together, power comes back about 11 hours sooner. Zone order is live on the MrGridy map. Stay safe.

title: Storm crew briefing: Helene (español)
text: Informes de cuadrilla para tormenta por el huracán Helene. Del lado de Georgia, se esperan los apagones más fuertes en el condado de Fulton, el condado de Richmond y el condado de Lowndes, con cerca de 802,000 clientes sin servicio en todo Georgia en el punto máximo. Del lado de Carolina del Sur, vigilen el condado de Greenville, el condado de Richland y el condado de Lexington, con cerca de 381,000 clientes sin servicio a nivel estatal. La simulación espera aproximadamente 1,100 secciones de transmisión dañadas en el sistema de Georgia Power y 140 en el de DESC. Ambas empresas de servicios públicos se apostarán conjuntamente en el puente de la I 520 sobre el río Savannah, que llega a una zona de reparación en 38 minutos, y en el puente de la I 95 sobre el río Savannah, que llega a cuatro zonas de reparación en 59 minutos. Las áreas vulnerables primero. Comiencen cerca del condado de Richmond, donde cerca de 5,000 residentes dependen de equipo médico con energía, luego el condado de Effingham y el condado de Coffee. Trabajando juntos, la energía regresa unas 11 horas antes. El orden de las zonas está activo en el mapa de MrGridy. Manténganse seguros.

title: Storm crew briefing: Irma
text: Storm crew briefing for Hurricane Irma. On the Georgia side, the heaviest outages are expected in Fulton County, Cobb County and Lowndes County, with about 257,000 customers out across Georgia at the peak. On the South Carolina side, watch Charleston County, Lexington County and Beaufort County, with about 65,000 customers out statewide. The simulation expects roughly 12 damaged transmission sections on Georgia Power's system and none on DESC's. No single yard reaches both sides quickly for this storm, so each utility stages on its own side and shares updates. Vulnerable areas first. Start near Bacon County, where about 180 residents rely on powered medical equipment, then Telfair County and Charlton County. Zone order is live on the MrGridy map. Stay safe.

title: Spark
text: a single subtle electric spark crackle, short and clean, close up, no music

title: Grid hum
text: a soft low electrical substation hum, steady and calm, seamless loop, no music
